title: Tensor compatibility of the canonical derived scalar/pullback comparison
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings and phi:R to A a unital homomorphism. Let f:X to Y be any morphism of schemes. Work in the unbounded derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write S_T for scalarExtension phi T, U_T for exact derived restriction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], F_R and F_A for derived inverse image, tau:S_Y followed by F_A isomorphic to F_R followed by S_X for the uniquely K-flat-normalized scalarPullbackIso, sigma_T: S_T followed by U_T isomorphic to tensoring on the right by scalarCoefficient phi T for scalarTensorIso [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection], and chi:U_Y followed by F_R isomorphic to F_A followed by U_X for scalarRestrictionPullbackIso [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. For every C in D(Y_et,R), chi_(S_Y C) followed by U_X(tau_C) followed by sigma_X(F_R C) equals F_R(sigma_Y(C)), followed by the canonical tensor/pullback comparison at (C,scalarCoefficient phi Y) [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], followed by tensoring id_(F_R C) with scalarCoefficientPullbackIso phi f. The coefficient isomorphism is the specified exact restriction/pullback comparison applied to the A-unit, with the exact single-complex and geometric unit comparisons. No boundedness, flatness of A over R, finiteness or properness assumption is made.

proof.text: Choose a cochain representative of C and a quasi-isomorphism P to it, with P K-flat and having flat terms. The resulting isomorphism Q(P) to C reduces the claim to Q(P), by naturality of every displayed comparison. Inverse image is exact and preserves K-flatness and flat terms.

The ordinary restriction/direct-image comparison is the identity and is monoidal: use Functor.isMonoidal_sheafPushforwardContinuousCompSheafComposeIso_hom for the base-change functor of small etale sites. Its inverse mate is the canonical restriction/pullback comparison chi, by underived_mate. That mate is monoidal, since its formula is a composite of monoidal geometric units, counits, associators and whiskerings. Taking the scalar mate of the inverse ordinary scalar/pullback comparison gives chi, by iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv and the definition of scalarSheafPullbackIso. Consequently FR(unit_Y M), followed by chi_(S_Y M) and U_X(tau_M), equals unit_X(FR M), by unit_mateEquiv and cancellation of tau inverse with tau. Expand scalarSheafTensorMap as scalar unit, lax restriction tensorator and right unitor. Naturality of chi, its monoidal tensor identity, the preceding unit equation, tensorator naturality and right unitality identify both ordinary tensor routes. The coefficient comparison that occurs is chi at the A-unit followed by restriction of the inverse geometric monoidal unit, precisely the one used in scalarCoefficientPullbackIso. The ordinary balancing map is an isomorphism: before sheafification its inverse sends a tensor m to m tensor a; the formulas respect scalar balancing and restriction, so they sheafify to inverse maps.

Apply the preceding sheaf equality degreewise to P and totalize. The coefficient factor is concentrated in degree zero, and no two degrees are exchanged, so both totalized maps carry the same signs. Apply Q. Substitute the defining representative equation of scalarPullbackIso at P and the two defining scalarTensorIso equations, at P and at its inverse image. Substitute the counit normalization leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison_app_app_comp and the exact-functor single-complex comparison for the coefficient sheaf. The source and target cochain model maps of the resulting equation are precisely those in the preceding totalized equality.

The geometric representative maps are invertible because inverse image is exact. The scalar-extension representative maps are invertible on the chosen K-flat models; the tensor model maps with K-flat first factor are invertible, even when A is not flat over R. Cancel these comparison maps in the localized equality from the preceding step. What remains is exactly chi_(S C), followed by U(tau_C) and sigma_X(F C), equal to F(sigma_Y C), followed by the tensor/pullback comparison and tensoring the specified coefficient identification. Transport through Q(P) isomorphic to C to finish. This proof uses no direct-image statement, properness, boundedness or finiteness.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarPullback_tensor_compatibility
    {R A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    (φ : R →+* A) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (C : DerivedCategoryModule R Y) :
    (scalarRestrictionPullbackIso φ f).hom.app ((scalarExtension φ Y).obj C) ≫
        (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars X.smallEtaleTopology φ).map
          ((scalarPullbackIso φ f).hom.app C) ≫
        (scalarTensorIso φ X).hom.app (L((f)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} R]).obj C) =
      L((f)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} R]).map ((scalarTensorIso φ Y).hom.app C) ≫
        ((leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) f).app C).app
          (scalarCoefficient φ Y) ≫
        ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X).obj
          (L((f)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} R]).obj C)).map
          (scalarCoefficientPullbackIso φ f).hom
